Based on my research, here are the U.S. assembly plant opening dates for each company:

## **Honda** (Company that invented/built VTEC technology)
- **November 1982** - Honda of America Mfg., Inc. opened in Marysville, Ohio (first Japanese automaker to build cars in America)
- December 1989 - East Liberty Auto Plant, Ohio (second U.S. auto plant)
- November 2001 - Honda Manufacturing of Alabama (third U.S. auto plant)
- October 2008 - Honda Manufacturing of Indiana (fourth U.S. auto plant)

## **Toyota** (Owner of the Scion brand)
- Toyota launched the Scion brand in **2003**, but Toyota's U.S. assembly history includes:
- 1986 - NUMMI joint venture plant in California (with GM) - started production
- 1988 - Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky (TMMK) opened
- 2006 - Toyota Motor Manufacturing Texas (San Antonio) opened
- 2007 - Toyota Motor Manufacturing Mississippi (Blue Springs) opened

Note: The original Scion models were assembled at Toyota's existing North American plants, primarily in California, Kentucky, Indiana, Texas, and Mississippi. Scion as a brand was discontinued in 2016 (though recently revived for a new kei truck being assembled in 2027).

## **Nissan**
- **June 16, 1983** - Nissan Motor Manufacturing Corporation USA began production at Smyrna, Tennessee (first vehicle rolled off the line; 1984 model year pickups began marketing in 1984)
- 1997 - Decherd, Tennessee powertrain plant opened
- 2003 - Canton, Mississippi vehicle assembly plant opened

---

### Summary Answer:
All three companies opened their U.S. auto assembly plants in the **early 1980s**:
- **Honda**: November 1982
- **Nissan**: June 1983  
- **Toyota**: 1986 (through NUMMI joint venture), with additional plants in 1988 and 2006+

In October 1946, Soichiro Honda established the Honda Technical Research Institute in Hamamatsu, Japan, to develop and produce small 2-cycle motorbike engines. Two years later, Honda Motor Company, Ltd. was born, and in 1959 Honda opened its first storefront in Los Angeles with six industrious employees.
From those simple beginnings in Los Angeles, American Honda has grown to become a top manufacturer of motorcycles, power equipment, ATVs, generators, marine engines, and of course, automobiles.
* * *

## Timeline
### 1974
The Honda Civic with groundbreaking CVCC engine is introduced; it's the first vehicle to satisfy the stringent new U.S. Clean Air Act without the use of a catalytic converter.

## Timeline
### 1976
The The Honda Accord debuts as a hatchback, followed by the Accord Sedan in 1979.

## Timeline

Civic CVCC tops the U.S. EPA's first-ever list of America's most fuel-efficient automobiles with an EPA fuel economy rating of 40 miles per gallon.

## Timeline
### 1982
Honda of America Mfg., Inc. begins producing the Accord at an all-new plant in Marysville, Ohio, making Honda the first Japanese automaker to build cars in America.*
Honda introduces the 1984 CRX-HF, the first car to achieve an EPA fuel economy rating in excess of 50 miles per gallon.

## Timeline
### 1986
Honda launches Acura, the first luxury nameplate from a Japanese automaker, with sales of the Integra sports sedan and its flagship Legend through 60 U.S. Acura dealers.

## Timeline
### 1988
The Honda Accord Coupe becomes the first-ever U.S.-built automobile to be exported from the U.S. to Japan.*

## Timeline
### 1989
Accord is the first vehicle from an international automaker to earn the title of America's best-selling automobile.
Honda's second U.S auto plant, in East Liberty, Ohio, begins production of Honda Civic vehicles.*

## Timeline
### 1990
The Acura NSX debuts as the world's first aluminum-bodied automobile and the first to employ Honda's now-legendary VTEC (Variable Timing and Left Electronic Control) engine technology.

## Timeline
### 1991
The 1991 Accord Wagon debuts as the first Honda vehicle to be designed, developed and manufactured in America.

## Timeline
### 1994

## Timeline

Honda Transmission Mfg. of America, Inc., begins production of automatic transmissions at a new plant in Russells Point, Ohio.

1998 Accord is the first automobile to meet California's Ultra-Low-Emission Vehicle (ULEV) exhaust emissions standards. American Honda begins leasing the Honda EV Plus, the first four-passenger battery-electric vehicle powered by advanced nickel-metal hydride batteries, and an early example of Honda's effort to advance Zero-Emissions Vehicle technology.

## Timeline
### 1998
Honda introduces the low-emission natural-gas powered Civic GX; in 2001 it is deemed the cleanest internal-combustion engine ever tested by the U.S. EPA.

## Timeline
### 1999
The original 2000 Honda Insight is launched as America's first gasoline-electric hybrid automobile and the most fuel-efficient automobile in America with an EPA rating of 70 miles per gallon.

## Timeline
### 2001
The U.S.-designed, -developed and -manufactured 2001 Civic Coupe is the first compact car in America to earn a 5-star safety rating from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) for both frontal and side impacts.
Honda Manufacturing of Alabama, LLC, begins production of Odyssey minivans at Honda's third U.S. auto plant, in Lincoln, Alabama. *It is the first auto plant in America to operate as a zero waste-to-landfill facility.
Honda is the first mass-market automaker to introduce an entire line of automobiles that meet or exceed California's LEV (Low-Emissions Vehicle) exhaust emissions standards.

## Timeline

The 2003 Civic Hybrid becomes Honda’s first mass-produced automobile to apply gasoline-electric powertrain technology.
The Honda FCX becomes the world’s first furel cell vehicles ceretifed by the U.S. EPA for everyday use.

## Timeline
### 2004
American Honda launches its industry-leading “Safety for Everyone” campaign to apply a core suite of advanced safety features to all Honda and Accura automobiles regardless of vehicles size or price.

## Timeline
### 2005
The Spallino family takes delivery of a Honda FCX, becoming the world’s first individual customer for a fuel cell car.

## Timeline
### 2006
Honda Precision Parts of Georgia, LLC, opens a new plant in Tallapoosa, Georgia, for the production of automobile transmissions.
Honda R&D Americas, Inc. opens its new Advanced Design Studio in Pasadena, California, to create advanced design concepts for future Honda and Acura vehicles

Honda commences production of the FCX Clarity in Japan on the world’s first production line dedicated to the manufacture of advanced, zero-emissions fuel cell vehicles. Lease sales begin for customers in Southern California.

_By John Linden_
It was October 1946, in Hamamatsu, Japan, when Soichiro Honda took over a factory wartime bombings had left in ruins; determined to succeed post war he established the Honda Technical Research Institute. Soichiro's first attempt at manufacturing was the "rotary weaving machine"; then he tried his hand at mass-producing frosted glass windows. After failing to "take off", and not one to give up, he next tried manufacturing woven bamboo roof panels. Then Soichiro came across a surplus of two-stroke motors and had an idea. With very little gasoline available for transportation, Soichiro decided to build motorbikes. Soichiro started adapting the small 2-cycle motorcycle engines to run on turpentine and attached them to cycle frames Hamamatsu factory workers built. The bikes were popular and soon sold out leading Soichiro to begin manufacturing his own engines; and the history of Honda began.

## 1946
*   Soichiro Honda takes over factory and establishes the Honda Technical Research Institute.  
*   Honda attempts manufacturing the "rotary weaving machine", frosted glass windows mass-production and woven bamboo roof panels.  
*   Honda adapts two-stroke motors to run on turpentine and attaches to flimsy bikes built in a Hamamatsu factory.  
*   Motorbikes are a huge success, in high demand and sell out.  
*   Soichiro begins manufacturing his own bike motors.

## 1947
*   Honda produces the first complete one-half horsepower A-type bicycle engine (nicknamed The Chimney due to being very smoky.)

## 1948
*   Honda Motor Company, Ltd. in incorporated.

## 1949
*   Honda manufactures the more sophisticated D-type; a steel-framed bike with front and rear suspension and speeds up to 50 miles per hour.

## Late 1950s
*   Honda introduces the Cub (Vespa clone).

## 1959
*   On June 11, the first Honda Motor Co., Ltd. overseas subsidiary storefront opened in Los Angeles with six employees.  
*   In September, the Los Angeles store begins selling three small motorcycle models, the Benley, Honda Dream and Super Cub (Honda 50).  
*   The Cub is the first Honda product sold in the U.S.

## 1962
*   Honda launches their ad campaign "You meet the nicest people on a Honda."  
*   Honda introduces power equipment to the United States and begins selling the F-19 mini-tiller.

## 1964
*   Honda introduces the U.S. to the E-40 and E-300 portable generators.

## 1969
*   Honda debuts the Honda Dream CB750 Four in the United States.  
*   The first Honda automobile (Honda N600) is sold in America.

## 1973
*   Honda introduces the world's first quieter, clearer and fuel-efficient 4-stroke outboard marine motors.  
*   As the first American energy crisis hits, Honda debuts its fuel-efficient Civic Hatchback.

## 1974
*   Honda introduces the Honda Civic equipped with a CVCC motor and without a catalytic converter. This groundbreaking technology is the first to meet the new stringent U.S. Clean Air Act regulations.

## 1975
*   Honda opens the Honda Research California in Gardenia, California and begins research and development in the U.S.

## 1976
*   Honda debuts the Accord hatchback.

## 1977
*   Introduces the GL1100 Gold Wing motorcycle.  
*   U.S. EPA's most fuel-efficient vehicles (40 miles per gallon EPA rating) list debuts with the Honda Civic CVCC at the top of the list.

## 1979
*   Honda Accord is debuted.  
*   Using global and domestic sourced parts, Honda becomes the first Japanese automaker to manufacture products in the United States with production of the CR250M Elsinore motorcycles begins at Honda of America, Mfg., Inc. in Marysville, Ohio.

## 1982
*   Honda begins production of the Accord at its Honda of America Mfg., Inc. factory making Japanese automaker the first to manufacture cars in the U.S.

## 1984
*   The Honda introduces the CRX-HF, the first EPA fuel economy rating of 50 miles per gallon.  
*   Production of walk-behind lawnmowers begins at the new Honda Power Equipment Mfg., Inc. plant in Swepsonville, North Carolina.

## 1985
*   Honda's new plant, Honda of America Mfg., Inc. opens and begins motorcycle engines production in Anna, Ohio.  
*   Engineering and development of new Acura and Honda automobiles, Honda power equipment and motorcycles begins at the new Honda R&D Americas, Inc. Ohio Center opens.

## 1986
*   In September, the Anna Engine plant manufactures its first automobile motor.  
*   Honda is the first Japanese automaker to launch a luxury nameplate in America, selling the Acura Integra sports sedan and Legend at 60 U.S. Acura dealers.

## 1988
*   The Honda Accord Coupe is the first ever U.S. manufactured automobile exported to Japan.

## 1989
*   The Accord becomes the first international vehicle to earn America's best-selling car title.  
*   Production of Honda Civic vehicles begins at Honda's second American automobile plant in East Liberty, Ohio.

## 1990
*   The Acura NSX equipped with the world's first, and Honda's now legendary Variable Timing and Lift Electronic Control (VTEC®) engine technology and an aluminum body debuts.

## 1991
*   Designed, developed and produced in the United States, the Accord Wagon debuts.

## 1994

_By John Linden_
It was October 1946, in Hamamatsu, Japan, when Soichiro Honda took over a factory wartime bombings had left in ruins; determined to succeed post war he established the Honda Technical Research Institute. Soichiro's first attempt at manufacturing was the "rotary weaving machine"; then he tried his hand at mass-producing frosted glass windows. After failing to "take off", and not one to give up, he next tried manufacturing woven bamboo roof panels. Then Soichiro came across a surplus of two-stroke motors and had an idea. With very little gasoline available for transportation, Soichiro decided to build motorbikes. Soichiro started adapting the small 2-cycle motorcycle engines to run on turpentine and attached them to cycle frames Hamamatsu factory workers built. The bikes were popular and soon sold out leading Soichiro to begin manufacturing his own engines; and the history of Honda began.

In October 1946, Soichiro Honda established the Honda Technical Research Institute in Hamamatsu, Japan, to develop and produce small 2-cycle motorbike engines. Two years later, Honda Motor Company, Ltd. was born, and in 1959 Honda opened its first storefront in Los Angeles with six industrious employees.
From those simple beginnings in Los Angeles, American Honda has grown to become a top manufacturer of motorcycles, power equipment, ATVs, generators, marine engines, and of course, automobiles.

It was October 1946, in Hamamatsu, Japan, when Soichiro Honda took over a factory wartime bombings had left in ruins; determined to succeed post war he established the Honda Technical Research Institute. Soichiro's first attempt at manufacturing was the "rotary weaving machine"; then he tried his hand at mass-producing frosted glass windows. After failing to "take off", and not one to give up, he next tried manufacturing woven bamboo roof panels. Then Soichiro came across a surplus of two-stroke motors and had an idea. With very little gasoline available for transportation, Soichiro decided to build motorbikes. Soichiro started adapting the small 2-cycle motorcycle engines to run on turpentine and attached them to cycle frames Hamamatsu factory workers built. The bikes were popular and soon sold out leading Soichiro to begin manufacturing his own engines; and the history of Honda began.

## 1946
*   Soichiro Honda takes over factory and establishes the Honda Technical Research Institute.  
*   Honda attempts manufacturing the "rotary weaving machine", frosted glass windows mass-production and woven bamboo roof panels.  
*   Honda adapts two-stroke motors to run on turpentine and attaches to flimsy bikes built in a Hamamatsu factory.  
*   Motorbikes are a huge success, in high demand and sell out.  
*   Soichiro begins manufacturing his own bike motors.

# Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01 - Toyota USA Newsroom
## Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01
**The KEI-01: Where the Journey Begins**
The KEI-01 is the first manifestation of the Scion by Toyota vision.
Providing the functionality, efficiency and versatility of Japan’s legendary kei trucks, the KEI-01 brings a proven concept to American customers in a packaged way that only Toyota companies can deliver. Designed to meet applicable low-speed vehicle federal safety requirements, the KEI-01 comes standard with a 660cc three-cylinder engine, a continuously variable transmission, and four-wheel drive (4WD) making it an affordable, highly capable, and remarkably maneuverable package.
Toyota has long focused on bringing customers vehicles that fit the way they live and work.For decades, kei trucks have earned a strong reputation in Japan and some other Asian markets for their practicality and versatility. The KEI-01 brings that combination to a new audience while challenging the traditional blueprint, giving customers the freedom to make it their own.
That spirit of going beyond blueprints, combined with Toyota’s commitment to “Fun to Drive,” makes the KEI-01 a natural first expression of the Scion by Toyota brand.
**Bringing the KEI-01 to Customers**
As an intentionally low-volume, niche vehicle, the KEI-01 will initially be offered through a fleet-focused pilot program to help the company learn how it can best serve U.S. customers and use cases. Initial fleet sales are planned through Scion by Toyota dealers selected from current Toyota dealers, which will serve as the customer-facing sales channel. Based on market conditions, customer demand, and operational considerations, Toyota may consider expanding availability to limited retail sales at a later date.
Additional information and the broader sales strategy will be shared as plans are finalized.
**Three Vehicles. Three Ways to go Beyond.**
While the KEI-01 is designed to bring a unique form of utility to U.S. customers, the SxS and BKE concepts demonstrate the broader range of ideas Scion by Toyota is intended to explore.
**SxS Concept – Beyond Limits**

# Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01 - Toyota USA Newsroom
## Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01
First shown at the 2025 SEMA Show, the SxS Concept is a purpose-built side-by-side concept that reimagines the all-terrain vehicle for a new generation of outdoor enthusiasts. Developed by the company’s North American engineering team, the concept combines a high-output turbocharged four-cylinder hybrid powertrain producing more than 300 horsepower with a compact, purpose-built off-road package.
Designed for everything from spirited desert running to technical rock crawling, the SxS Concept features significant suspension articulation and a nimble footprint. It also features a Silent Mode that allows the vehicle to operate using electric power, offering a different way to experience the outdoors.
Representing Scion by Toyota’s willingness to take Toyota technology and engineering into entirely new spaces, the SxS Concept pushes beyond the limits of terrain, performance and what this kind of vehicle can be. The SxS Concept is more than an exercise in imagination. Toyota will continue advancing the concept, exploring its potential, and evaluating how it could bring an entirely new kind of off-road experience to enthusiasts.
**BKE Concept – Beyond Permission**
The BKE Concept explores another dimension of personal mobility, bringing together compact packaging, utility and adventure in a concept designed to expand the possibilities of how people move through and experience the outdoors.
Where the KEI-01 emphasizes practical utility and the SxS Concept showcases off-road performance, the BKE Concept opens up the space in between—offering freedom to choose your own direction, to take the unexpected turn, and explore beyond permission. Its small, highly adaptable form creates new possibilities for different lifestyles, activities and experiences.
Together, these three distinct vehicles illustrate the breadth of the Scion by Toyota laboratory: from everyday utility, to high-performance adventure, to entirely new forms of personal mobility.
**Assembled in America**
The KEI-01 will be assembled at Toyota Motor Manufacturing Indiana (Toyota Indiana) starting in the second half of 2027, supported by a $34 million investment that will add approximately 50 new jobs.

# Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01 - Toyota USA Newsroom
## Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01
Assembly at Toyota Indiana represents the company’s continued commitment to investing in the U.S. and American jobs. The investment will establish new vehicle assembly operations and upgrade production and logistics infrastructure, bringing this unique utility vehicle closer to U.S. customers.
**Small Footprint. Big Capability.**
Despite its compact footprint, the KEI-01 delivers capability, versatility and operator comfort. Key highlights include:
*   **Efficient Powertrain:** Powered by a proven 660cc three-cylinder engine mated to a continuously variable transmission, delivering a balance of low-end torque and exceptional fuel efficiency for all-day operation.  
*   **Rugged Drivetrain:** Standard selectable four-wheel drive (4WD) with auto mode and push-button lock up to help the KEI-01 tackle mud, snow and uneven terrain.  
*   **Versatile Cargo Access:** An easily accessible three-way fold-down cargo bed allows operators to load and unload materials from a lower height.  
*   **Extended Cabin Comfort:** An extended-cabin design with a raised roofline allows for reclining and sliding seats, plus secure interior storage behind the seats for tools and gear.  
*   **All-Weather Climate Control:** An enclosed cabin with heat and air conditioning helps keep operators comfortable throughout the year.  
*   **Maneuverable Footprint:** Measuring just over 11 feet in length and under 5 feet in width, the KEI-01 offers exceptional agility and maneuverability in tight spaces.  
*   **Impressive Payload and Towing:** A payload capacity of up to 600 pounds in the bed and structural rigidity for towing small trailers and equipment make it a versatile utility performer.
**Built for Work, Play and Everything in Between**
The KEI-01 will provide customers with a practical, right-sized solution for buyers who need versatility and durability without the size or expense of a traditional pickup.
The KEI-01 is a right-hand-drive vehicle designed to comply with FMVSS No. 500 requirements for LSVs. Its maximum speed will be 25 miles per hour.

## Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01
**The KEI-01: Where the Journey Begins**
The KEI-01 is the first manifestation of the Scion by Toyota vision.
Providing the functionality, efficiency and versatility of Japan’s legendary kei trucks, the KEI-01 brings a proven concept to American customers in a packaged way that only Toyota companies can deliver. Designed to meet applicable low-speed vehicle federal safety requirements, the KEI-01 comes standard with a 660cc three-cylinder engine, a continuously variable transmission, and four-wheel drive (4WD) making it an affordable, highly capable, and remarkably maneuverable package.
Toyota has long focused on bringing customers vehicles that fit the way they live and work.For decades, kei trucks have earned a strong reputation in Japan and some other Asian markets for their practicality and versatility. The KEI-01 brings that combination to a new audience while challenging the traditional blueprint, giving customers the freedom to make it their own.
That spirit of going beyond blueprints, combined with Toyota’s commitment to “Fun to Drive,” makes the KEI-01 a natural first expression of the Scion by Toyota brand.
**Bringing the KEI-01 to Customers**
As an intentionally low-volume, niche vehicle, the KEI-01 will initially be offered through a fleet-focused pilot program to help the company learn how it can best serve U.S. customers and use cases. Initial fleet sales are planned through Scion by Toyota dealers selected from current Toyota dealers, which will serve as the customer-facing sales channel. Based on market conditions, customer demand, and operational considerations, Toyota may consider expanding availability to limited retail sales at a later date.
Additional information and the broader sales strategy will be shared as plans are finalized.
**Three Vehicles. Three Ways to go Beyond.**
While the KEI-01 is designed to bring a unique form of utility to U.S. customers, the SxS and BKE concepts demonstrate the broader range of ideas Scion by Toyota is intended to explore.

# Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01 - Toyota USA Newsroom
## Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01
First shown at the 2025 SEMA Show, the SxS Concept is a purpose-built side-by-side concept that reimagines the all-terrain vehicle for a new generation of outdoor enthusiasts. Developed by the company’s North American engineering team, the concept combines a high-output turbocharged four-cylinder hybrid powertrain producing more than 300 horsepower with a compact, purpose-built off-road package.
Designed for everything from spirited desert running to technical rock crawling, the SxS Concept features significant suspension articulation and a nimble footprint. It also features a Silent Mode that allows the vehicle to operate using electric power, offering a different way to experience the outdoors.
Representing Scion by Toyota’s willingness to take Toyota technology and engineering into entirely new spaces, the SxS Concept pushes beyond the limits of terrain, performance and what this kind of vehicle can be. The SxS Concept is more than an exercise in imagination. Toyota will continue advancing the concept, exploring its potential, and evaluating how it could bring an entirely new kind of off-road experience to enthusiasts.
**BKE Concept – Beyond Permission**
The BKE Concept explores another dimension of personal mobility, bringing together compact packaging, utility and adventure in a concept designed to expand the possibilities of how people move through and experience the outdoors.
Where the KEI-01 emphasizes practical utility and the SxS Concept showcases off-road performance, the BKE Concept opens up the space in between—offering freedom to choose your own direction, to take the unexpected turn, and explore beyond permission. Its small, highly adaptable form creates new possibilities for different lifestyles, activities and experiences.
Together, these three distinct vehicles illustrate the breadth of the Scion by Toyota laboratory: from everyday utility, to high-performance adventure, to entirely new forms of personal mobility.
**Assembled in America**
The KEI-01 will be assembled at Toyota Motor Manufacturing Indiana (Toyota Indiana) starting in the second half of 2027, supported by a $34 million investment that will add approximately 50 new jobs.

# Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01 - Toyota USA Newsroom
## Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01
Assembly at Toyota Indiana represents the company’s continued commitment to investing in the U.S. and American jobs. The investment will establish new vehicle assembly operations and upgrade production and logistics infrastructure, bringing this unique utility vehicle closer to U.S. customers.
**Small Footprint. Big Capability.**
Despite its compact footprint, the KEI-01 delivers capability, versatility and operator comfort. Key highlights include:
*   **Efficient Powertrain:** Powered by a proven 660cc three-cylinder engine mated to a continuously variable transmission, delivering a balance of low-end torque and exceptional fuel efficiency for all-day operation.  
*   **Rugged Drivetrain:** Standard selectable four-wheel drive (4WD) with auto mode and push-button lock up to help the KEI-01 tackle mud, snow and uneven terrain.  
*   **Versatile Cargo Access:** An easily accessible three-way fold-down cargo bed allows operators to load and unload materials from a lower height.  
*   **Extended Cabin Comfort:** An extended-cabin design with a raised roofline allows for reclining and sliding seats, plus secure interior storage behind the seats for tools and gear.  
*   **All-Weather Climate Control:** An enclosed cabin with heat and air conditioning helps keep operators comfortable throughout the year.  
*   **Maneuverable Footprint:** Measuring just over 11 feet in length and under 5 feet in width, the KEI-01 offers exceptional agility and maneuverability in tight spaces.  
*   **Impressive Payload and Towing:** A payload capacity of up to 600 pounds in the bed and structural rigidity for towing small trailers and equipment make it a versatile utility performer.
**Built for Work, Play and Everything in Between**
The KEI-01 will provide customers with a practical, right-sized solution for buyers who need versatility and durability without the size or expense of a traditional pickup.
The KEI-01 is a right-hand-drive vehicle designed to comply with FMVSS No. 500 requirements for LSVs. Its maximum speed will be 25 miles per hour.

## Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01
**The KEI-01: Where the Journey Begins**
The KEI-01 is the first manifestation of the Scion by Toyota vision.
Providing the functionality, efficiency and versatility of Japan’s legendary kei trucks, the KEI-01 brings a proven concept to American customers in a packaged way that only Toyota companies can deliver. Designed to meet applicable low-speed vehicle federal safety requirements, the KEI-01 comes standard with a 660cc three-cylinder engine, a continuously variable transmission, and four-wheel drive (4WD) making it an affordable, highly capable, and remarkably maneuverable package.
Toyota has long focused on bringing customers vehicles that fit the way they live and work.For decades, kei trucks have earned a strong reputation in Japan and some other Asian markets for their practicality and versatility. The KEI-01 brings that combination to a new audience while challenging the traditional blueprint, giving customers the freedom to make it their own.
That spirit of going beyond blueprints, combined with Toyota’s commitment to “Fun to Drive,” makes the KEI-01 a natural first expression of the Scion by Toyota brand.
**Bringing the KEI-01 to Customers**
As an intentionally low-volume, niche vehicle, the KEI-01 will initially be offered through a fleet-focused pilot program to help the company learn how it can best serve U.S. customers and use cases. Initial fleet sales are planned through Scion by Toyota dealers selected from current Toyota dealers, which will serve as the customer-facing sales channel. Based on market conditions, customer demand, and operational considerations, Toyota may consider expanding availability to limited retail sales at a later date.
Additional information and the broader sales strategy will be shared as plans are finalized.
**Three Vehicles. Three Ways to go Beyond.**
While the KEI-01 is designed to bring a unique form of utility to U.S. customers, the SxS and BKE concepts demonstrate the broader range of ideas Scion by Toyota is intended to explore.

## Toyota Says ‘Okei’ to America: Introducing the Scion by Toyota Brand and KEI-01
First shown at the 2025 SEMA Show, the SxS Concept is a purpose-built side-by-side concept that reimagines the all-terrain vehicle for a new generation of outdoor enthusiasts. Developed by the company’s North American engineering team, the concept combines a high-output turbocharged four-cylinder hybrid powertrain producing more than 300 horsepower with a compact, purpose-built off-road package.
Designed for everything from spirited desert running to technical rock crawling, the SxS Concept features significant suspension articulation and a nimble footprint. It also features a Silent Mode that allows the vehicle to operate using electric power, offering a different way to experience the outdoors.
Representing Scion by Toyota’s willingness to take Toyota technology and engineering into entirely new spaces, the SxS Concept pushes beyond the limits of terrain, performance and what this kind of vehicle can be. The SxS Concept is more than an exercise in imagination. Toyota will continue advancing the concept, exploring its potential, and evaluating how it could bring an entirely new kind of off-road experience to enthusiasts.
**BKE Concept – Beyond Permission**
The BKE Concept explores another dimension of personal mobility, bringing together compact packaging, utility and adventure in a concept designed to expand the possibilities of how people move through and experience the outdoors.
Where the KEI-01 emphasizes practical utility and the SxS Concept showcases off-road performance, the BKE Concept opens up the space in between—offering freedom to choose your own direction, to take the unexpected turn, and explore beyond permission. Its small, highly adaptable form creates new possibilities for different lifestyles, activities and experiences.
Together, these three distinct vehicles illustrate the breadth of the Scion by Toyota laboratory: from everyday utility, to high-performance adventure, to entirely new forms of personal mobility.
**Assembled in America**
The KEI-01 will be assembled at Toyota Motor Manufacturing Indiana (Toyota Indiana) starting in the second half of 2027, supported by a $34 million investment that will add approximately 50 new jobs.

Assembly at Toyota Indiana represents the company’s continued commitment to investing in the U.S. and American jobs. The investment will establish new vehicle assembly operations and upgrade production and logistics infrastructure, bringing this unique utility vehicle closer to U.S. customers.
**Small Footprint. Big Capability.**
Despite its compact footprint, the KEI-01 delivers capability, versatility and operator comfort. Key highlights include:
*   **Efficient Powertrain:** Powered by a proven 660cc three-cylinder engine mated to a continuously variable transmission, delivering a balance of low-end torque and exceptional fuel efficiency for all-day operation.  
*   **Rugged Drivetrain:** Standard selectable four-wheel drive (4WD) with auto mode and push-button lock up to help the KEI-01 tackle mud, snow and uneven terrain.  
*   **Versatile Cargo Access:** An easily accessible three-way fold-down cargo bed allows operators to load and unload materials from a lower height.  
*   **Extended Cabin Comfort:** An extended-cabin design with a raised roofline allows for reclining and sliding seats, plus secure interior storage behind the seats for tools and gear.  
*   **All-Weather Climate Control:** An enclosed cabin with heat and air conditioning helps keep operators comfortable throughout the year.  
*   **Maneuverable Footprint:** Measuring just over 11 feet in length and under 5 feet in width, the KEI-01 offers exceptional agility and maneuverability in tight spaces.  
*   **Impressive Payload and Towing:** A payload capacity of up to 600 pounds in the bed and structural rigidity for towing small trailers and equipment make it a versatile utility performer.
**Built for Work, Play and Everything in Between**
The KEI-01 will provide customers with a practical, right-sized solution for buyers who need versatility and durability without the size or expense of a traditional pickup.

## Innovation that excites. Since 1914.
Though the first Nissan – actually a Datsun – was produced in 1914, the name Nissan itself didn’t truly debut until 1933 when founder Yoshisuke Aikawa listed the Nihon Sangyo Company on the Tokyo Stock Exchange under the ticker name: NISSAN. In the more than 90 years since, the Nissan name has grown to be known in almost every corner of the Globe.
THE STORY BEGINS

## Origins of Nissan
The global automotive manufacturer, known today as Nissan, first debuted in 1911 when the Kwaishinsha (Kaishinsha) Motor Car Works was founded in Tokyo. 3 years later its first DAT model — an acronym of the initial investors surnames — was produced.

## 1914-1959
1933 Nissan Motor Co., Ltd., is established in Japan.
1937

## 1914-1959
### Japan's first mass-produced vehicle
The Datsun Type 15 was the first mass-produced Japanese vehicle. Other Type 15 models included Phaeton, mini pickup and delivery van.
1957

## 1914-1959
### The Nissan Skyline debuts
A forerunner to the revolutionary GT-R®, the Skyline was introduced in 1957. The modern Nissan R35 GT-R was first made for sale in the U.S. in 2009.
1958

## 1914-1959
### Datsun comes to America
The first Datsun introduced to the U.S. market in 1958 was the Datsun 1000, built on the same platform as the Datsun pickup truck. This was replaced in 1961 by the Datsun 1200 pictured here.
1959

## 1914-1959
### Building a solid reputation
In 1959, the compact pickup truck came to America. While the first Datsun models arrived in '58, the next year a quarter-ton model with a 48-HP 1200 CC engine established itself on American shores.

## NISSAN INNOVATION DEBUTS IN AMERICA IN 1959
From Japan to America
Nissan brought its first Datsuns (a 1000 cc car and truck) to the U.S. at the 1959 Los Angeles Auto Show. Over the years to keep up with growing global demand, Nissan started production in Mexico in 1966. Production in Australia and Taiwan followed, with the first American factory opening in Smyrna, Tennessee, in 1983.

## 1960-1969
Datsun performance shines
1961

## 1960-1969
### Fairlady 1200 Roadster
The first Datsun sports car imported to the U.S. This convertible roadster was built with steel bodywork with a 48-hp and drum brakes, zippy for the time. 288 units were produced through 1962.
1965

## 1960-1969
### Datsun 320 Truck
An upgrade to previous Datsun trucks, the 320 had a 60-hp engine and the first 4-speed floor shifter. The pictured vehicle was found in the Arizona desert and restored by Classic Datsun of Vista, CA.
1967

## 1960-1969
### Exclusive performance
Highly desired by collectors, the 2000 Roadster was the first Japanese production sports car to come with a 5-speed. That, plus its robust 150-hp engine, made it extra fun to drive. Production was limited to 1,000, and the first 10 were light-weight versions for racing.
1967

## 1960-1969
### Nissan 411 4-Door Sedan
Designed by Italian design house, Pininfarina, 411 featured a luxurious interior. An upmarket car in Japan, sales were slowed by a higher MSRP. This was the first Datsun vehicle in the American market to feature a fully 3-speed automatic transmission.
1967

## 1960-1969
### Nissan Patrol
Nissan's first SUV in the U.S. followed Land Rover’s trail and offered more power for less, but just as tough. The Patrol was the only vehicle sold and marketed in the U.S. as a Nissan prior to 1983.
1968

## 1960-1969
### American inspired
Nissan launched the first car styled for the U.S. market, the Datsun 510 sedan, in 2-door, 4-door and a 5-door wagon.
1969

## 1960-1969
### Datsun® 1600 Roadster
The Datsun 1600 Roadster debuted in 1964-1965 as the Datsun Fairlady 1500 and shared many mechanical features with the Datsun Bluebird. Eventually, the model evolved into the Fairlady 1600 Roadster.
The 70s were a great decade for Nissan. Nissan sold the one-millionth Datsun and became the top vehicle importer in the United States by 1975.

## NISSAN DESIGN COMES TO AMERICA
Driving innovation
In 1971, annual sales eclipsed 250,000 in the United States for the first time. Nissan also established itself on the track, as the now-legendary Datsun 510 and 240Z dominated racing on two continents. In 1973, the 1-Millionth Vehicle was sold in America. In 1979, Nissan Design America (NDA) was established in La Jolla, California, with a mandate to bring American style and concepts to Nissan vehicles. Over the years, NDA has brought us the original Altima®, the original Pathfinder®, the modular Pulsar NX, Xterra®.

## 1970-1979
Pushing the limits. Building a solid reputation
1971

## 1970-1979
### Datsun Coupe
The Datsun Coupe featured seating for five and "fold-down" rear seats. Available in the U.S. from 1970-73, selling 89,541 units making it the best-selling car of the time. Datsun 1200 Coupes won three SCCA C-Sedan National Championships.
1971

## 1970-1979
### Racing Datsun 510, #46
Peter Brock and Brock Racing Enterprises (BRE) built and raced the number 46 Datsun 510, which won the 1971 and 1972 SCCA Trans-Am championships driven by John Morton. Its success helped to bring brand recognition to a newcomer in the emerging Japanese market.
1971

## 1970-1979
### Datsun 240Z debut
240Z was introduced as a new sports car at the New York Auto Show in 1969. It featured a fastback styled body based on European design and boasted standard equipment, like a strong inline 2.4 liter 6-cylinder engine and full instrumentation reclining bucket seats at an affordable price.
1972

## 1970-1979
### Datsun 510® sedan
The 510® was a novel concept at the time: A good-looking, economical, fuel-efficient, five-passenger car that was fun to drive. It was available in a 4-door sedan or 2-door coupe with independent rear suspension or a 5-door wagon. Over its lifetime, the 510 went on to sell more than 300,000 units.
1977

## 1970-1979
### Datsun King Cab
Building a solid reputation for durable and fun-to-drive small trucks, Datsun introduced the King Cab, the first extended cab pickup, in 1977.
1978

## 1970-1979
### Datsun B210gx
The B210 was renowned as Nissan’s best-selling small sedan of the 1970s. The 1978 model was rated at 48 mpg highway, and the “B210 Plus” edition boasted 50 mpg highway – a lofty achievement for a carbureted vehicle.

## FROM TRUCKS TO THE RACETRACKS
Building off of success
Nissan built upon its successes of the 1970s – both in the showrooms and on the racetrack. Nissan Motor Manufacturing Corporation (NMMC) was established in Smyrna, Tennessee, to fulfill the growing demand for Nissan vehicles. In 1989, Nissan produced the 1-millionth vehicle on American soil. On the track, Hollywood legend Paul Newman captured Nissan's 50th national SCCA championship following consecutive wins in 1985 and 1986 with the Newman/Sharp Trans-Am 300ZX®.

## 1980-1989
Finding our stride, Building on racing legends.
1981

## 1980-1989
### 4-door Sports Car is born
The first-generation Nissan Maxima was introduced as the successor to the Datsun 810 sedan. Equipped with an inline-6 engine from the 240Z, this was no ordinary sedan and the Maxima cemented its 4-door sports car status for decades to come.
1982

## 1980-1989
### Championship off-road racing trucks
Between 1982 and 1992, Datsun collected an impressive 19 off-roading championship trophies.Nissan's most radical off-roader — a sandblasting 380-hp King Cab desert racer — competed in the HRDA/SCORE Class 1 Unlimited Vehicle series.
1983

## 1980-1989
### First American-built Nissan truck
The marketing of vehicles using Nissan badging in the U.S.began with the production of the 1984 Nissan pickup on June 16, 1983, at the new assembly plant in Smyrna, Tennessee. Early models carried dual Datsun-Nissan branding to help consumers make the change.
1985

## 1980-1989
### First Sentra® built in America
The first-generation Nissan Sentra was introduced in 1982 as a replacement for the popular and economical B210. It was so popular in the U.S. that in 1985, Sentra became the second Nissan model to roll off the line in the U.S in Smyrna, Tennessee.
1988

## 1980-1989
### The stellar Nissan racing record
Nissan racing driver Geoff Brabham won his first of four consecutive IMSA Camel GT Driver’s Championships. Brabham’s IMSA GTP ZX-T car was practically unbeatable that year, clocking a breathtaking top speed of 200+ miles per hour on several tracks and winning eight consecutive races.

## Leaping Into Green Tech
Retaining the best of Nissan
In 1991, Nissan received its first environmental award from the EPA,taking a big leap forward in green technology by lending its Alternative Fuel Vehicle to a California testing program and introducing the Future Electric Vehicle concept car. In 1997, Nissan was named “Best of the Best” by the Environmental Protection Agency. 1992 marked the sale of the 2-millionth Nissan Sentra in the United States, an additional accomplishment.

## 1990-1999
A decade of agility and innovation.
1993

## 1990-1999
### First Altima assembled in America
The Nissan Altima was introduced to replace the discontinued Stanza line. U.S.-assembled in Smyrna, Tennessee, it made an immediate impact in the mid-size sedan segment which continues today with its sixth-generation.
1995

## 1990-1999
### Compact without compromise
1995 was the year Nissan introduced the world to the all-new 200SX® coupe and the all-new 4th-generation Sentra.
1999

## 1990-1999
### The first 4-door compact truck
In 1999, Nissan introduced the Frontier® Crew Cab, the first compact truck with four full-sized doors. That same year, Frontier, Xterra® and Pathfinder® were named the official vehicles of the Los Angeles County lifeguards, which made many appearances in the T.V. show “Baywatch.”
GROWING LINE-UP

## 21st-Century thrills
Nissan nearly doubled the number of models offered and its sales. In 10 years, the diverse lineup grew to include the first full-size Nissan truck, along with all-new hybrid technology and a 21st-century supercar. And this is only the beginning of what's to come.

## 2000-2009
A new century of excitement.
2003

## 2000-2009
### Z Resurrected
The Nissan 350Z, a two-door, two-seater sports car, kicked off production in 2002 and ended the 6-year production hiatus in the US. Its sleek redesign of the 240Z DNA, rejuvenated the Nissan market presence throughout the decade.
2005

## 2000-2009
### Off-road innovation
An all-new midsize Frontier® launched with the most powerful V6 in its class. Nissan also introduced a mid-sized Pathfinder® with an added 3rd-row of seating, and the 2nd-generation Xterra® made its debut.
2007

## 2000-2009
### Nissan's first hybrid
In 2007, Nissan offered a hybrid driving option for the first time ever with the introduction of the all-new Altima® Hybrid.
2009

## 2000-2009
### The legend lands
Nissan brought its legendary GT-R to the U.S as an affordable supercar. With amazing acceleration, all-wheel drive, aggressive handling and bold styling, it has become an icon in the U.S. sports car market.
2009

## 2000-2009
### The shape of things
The boxy yet stylish Nissan Cube® made its North American debut with its non-traditional, asymmetrical body.
TRADITION OF INNOVATION

## The first Nissan EV
Nissan helped to lead the automotive industry into the age of electric vehicles when it debuted the all-electric Nissan LEAF®. Throughout the decade, Nissan continued its tradition of innovation that excites with all-new vehicles like the Nissan Kicks and with safety technology like its available Safety Shield® 360 suite of features.

## 2010-2020
The dawn of Nissan electrification
2010

## 2010-2020
### Nissan LEAF®
In 2010, Nissan introduced Nissan LEAF®—the world’s first mass-produced, 100% electric, zero-emission automobile. The standard 24-kWh battery was replaced with a 30-kWh battery for 2016, featuring 107 miles of range. The 2018 LEAF introduced an all-new design and a 40-kWh battery that took range up to 151 miles, and in 2019, LEAF PLUS added an available 60-kWh battery, estimated by EPA to offer up to 226 miles of range.
2018

## 2010-2020
### Nissan Kicks: The crossover of self expression
The Nissan Kicks made its North American debut as an affordable entry in the fast-growing subcompact crossover segment. Redesigned for 2025, the Kicks grew in size and adopted new styling inside and out, along with a more powerful engine and available Intelligent All-Wheel Drive.
2019

## 2010-2020
### Nissan Altima: All-Wheel Drive sedan
Continuing the Altima tradition of innovation in the sedan market, the Nissan Altima offered an available Intelligent All-Wheel Drive system for the first time. And it's still available today.
Nissan Goes Electric

## 2010-2020
### The All-Electric 2026 Nissan LEAF®
Discover a sleek, aerodynamic design engineered for efficiency and performance. Innovation meets power in every detail of this all-electric vehicle.

# 40 years of people, product and purpose
Nissan marks four decades of U.S. manufacturing; prepares for ‘electrified’ future

May 17, 2023
**NASHVILLE, Tenn.** – The story began on June 16, 1983, when the first Nissan manufactured in the U.S.− a white 720 pickup − rolled off the assembly line in Smyrna, marking the genesis of automotive production in Tennessee.
Nissan has since expanded its U.S. footprint to include a powertrain plant in Decherd, Tennessee in 1997 and a vehicle assembly plant in Canton, Mississippi in 2003. Collectively, these facilities have proudly built 1 nearly 20 million vehicles and 13 million engines in the U.S. for customers around the globe.
"What began with one pickup truck has turned into four decades of manufacturing excellence," said Nissan Americas Chairperson Jérémie Papin. "This milestone isn't just about the products we've built and sold over the past 40 years. It's also about applauding Nissan's more than 21,000 U.S. employees who will take us into our future − our electrified future − and continue to enhance our products and services for customers."
**Stronger communities**
Nissan prides itself on being supportive of its neighbors and helping to build stronger communities. Over the past 40 years, the company and its manufacturing team members have positively impacted communities through charitable contributions and volunteerism, including:
*   **43,000** volunteer hours  
*   **38**homes constructed with Habitat for Humanity  
*   Nearly **$26,000,000** in United Way donations  
*   Nearly **$2,000,000** in educational scholarships  
*   **36,000** pints of blood donated to the American Red Cross
**Electrified future**

# 40 years of people, product and purpose
The vehicles of the near future are connected and electric. Nissan is supporting that transition by building factories of the future today as part of its long-term vision, Ambition 2030**, which includes plans for 27 electrified models globally, including 19 all-electric vehicles, by 2030.**
**In 2022, Nissan**announced**a $500 million investment to transform its**Canton, Mississippi facility into a center for U.S. EV production to support two all-new, all-electric vehicles in 2025. This investment is one of several the company is planning in the U.S. over the next five years, supporting its target of 40% of U.S. vehicle sales to be fully electric, by 2030.
To learn more about Nissan's U.S. manufacturing operations, visit the company's newly launched website www.NissanManufacturing.com.

For more information about our products, services and commitment to sustainable mobility, visitnissanusa.com. You can also follow us onFacebook,Instagram,TwitterandLinkedInand see all our latest videos onYouTube.

# 40 years of people, product and purpose
Nissan marks four decades of U.S. manufacturing; prepares for ‘electrified’ future
[Save](javascript:void(0) "Add to Saved Items")[Remove](javascript:void(0) "Remove from Saved Items")DownloadShare
Subscribe
Photos / Galleries / Videos
May 17, 2023
**NASHVILLE, Tenn.** – The story began on June 16, 1983, when the first Nissan manufactured in the U.S.− a white 720 pickup − rolled off the assembly line in Smyrna, marking the genesis of automotive production in Tennessee.
Nissan has since expanded its U.S. footprint to include a powertrain plant in Decherd, Tennessee in 1997 and a vehicle assembly plant in Canton, Mississippi in 2003. Collectively, these facilities have proudly built 1 nearly 20 million vehicles and 13 million engines in the U.S. for customers around the globe.
"What began with one pickup truck has turned into four decades of manufacturing excellence," said Nissan Americas Chairperson Jérémie Papin. "This milestone isn't just about the products we've built and sold over the past 40 years. It's also about applauding Nissan's more than 21,000 U.S. employees who will take us into our future − our electrified future − and continue to enhance our products and services for customers."
**Stronger communities**
Nissan prides itself on being supportive of its neighbors and helping to build stronger communities. Over the past 40 years, the company and its manufacturing team members have positively impacted communities through charitable contributions and volunteerism, including:
*   **43,000** volunteer hours  
*   **38**homes constructed with Habitat for Humanity  
*   Nearly **$26,000,000** in United Way donations  
*   Nearly **$2,000,000** in educational scholarships  
*   **36,000** pints of blood donated to the American Red Cross
**Electrified future**

# 40 years of people, product and purpose
The vehicles of the near future are connected and electric. Nissan is supporting that transition by building factories of the future today as part of its long-term vision, Ambition 2030**, which includes plans for 27 electrified models globally, including 19 all-electric vehicles, by 2030.**
**In 2022, Nissan**announced**a $500 million investment to transform its**Canton, Mississippi facility into a center for U.S. EV production to support two all-new, all-electric vehicles in 2025. This investment is one of several the company is planning in the U.S. over the next five years, supporting its target of 40% of U.S. vehicle sales to be fully electric, by 2030.
To learn more about Nissan's U.S. manufacturing operations, visit the company's newly launched website www.NissanManufacturing.com.

## Innovation that excites. Since 1914.
Though the first Nissan – actually a Datsun – was produced in 1914, the name Nissan itself didn’t truly debut until 1933 when founder Yoshisuke Aikawa listed the Nihon Sangyo Company on the Tokyo Stock Exchange under the ticker name: NISSAN. In the more than 90 years since, the Nissan name has grown to be known in almost every corner of the Globe.
THE STORY BEGINS
texts.1:
## Origins of Nissan
The global automotive manufacturer, known today as Nissan, first debuted in 1911 when the Kwaishinsha (Kaishinsha) Motor Car Works was founded in Tokyo. 3 years later its first DAT model — an acronym of the initial investors surnames — was produced.
texts.2:
## 1914-1959
1933 Nissan Motor Co., Ltd., is established in Japan.
1937
texts.3:
## 1914-1959
### Japan's first mass-produced vehicle
The Datsun Type 15 was the first mass-produced Japanese vehicle. Other Type 15 models included Phaeton, mini pickup and delivery van.
1957
texts.4:
## 1914-1959
### The Nissan Skyline debuts
A forerunner to the revolutionary GT-R®, the Skyline was introduced in 1957. The modern Nissan R35 GT-R was first made for sale in the U.S. in 2009.
1958
texts.5:
## 1914-1959
### Datsun comes to America
The first Datsun introduced to the U.S. market in 1958 was the Datsun 1000, built on the same platform as the Datsun pickup truck. This was replaced in 1961 by the Datsun 1200 pictured here.
1959
texts.6:
## 1914-1959
### Building a solid reputation
In 1959, the compact pickup truck came to America. While the first Datsun models arrived in '58, the next year a quarter-ton model with a 48-HP 1200 CC engine established itself on American shores.
texts.7:
## NISSAN INNOVATION DEBUTS IN AMERICA IN 1959
From Japan to America
Nissan brought its first Datsuns (a 1000 cc car and truck) to the U.S. at the 1959 Los Angeles Auto Show. Over the years to keep up with growing global demand, Nissan started production in Mexico in 1966. Production in Australia and Taiwan followed, with the first American factory opening in Smyrna, Tennessee, in 1983.
texts.9:
## 1960-1969
### Fairlady 1200 Roadster
The first Datsun sports car imported to the U.S. This convertible roadster was built with steel bodywork with a 48-hp and drum brakes, zippy for the time. 288 units were produced through 1962.
1965
texts.10:
## 1960-1969
### Datsun 320 Truck
An upgrade to previous Datsun trucks, the 320 had a 60-hp engine and the first 4-speed floor shifter. The pictured vehicle was found in the Arizona desert and restored by Classic Datsun of Vista, CA.
1967
texts.11:
## 1960-1969
### Exclusive performance
Highly desired by collectors, the 2000 Roadster was the first Japanese production sports car to come with a 5-speed. That, plus its robust 150-hp engine, made it extra fun to drive. Production was limited to 1,000, and the first 10 were light-weight versions for racing.
1967
texts.12:
## 1960-1969
### Nissan 411 4-Door Sedan
Designed by Italian design house, Pininfarina, 411 featured a luxurious interior. An upmarket car in Japan, sales were slowed by a higher MSRP. This was the first Datsun vehicle in the American market to feature a fully 3-speed automatic transmission.
1967
texts.13:
## 1960-1969
### Nissan Patrol
Nissan's first SUV in the U.S. followed Land Rover’s trail and offered more power for less, but just as tough. The Patrol was the only vehicle sold and marketed in the U.S. as a Nissan prior to 1983.
1968
texts.14:
## 1960-1969
### American inspired
Nissan launched the first car styled for the U.S. market, the Datsun 510 sedan, in 2-door, 4-door and a 5-door wagon.
1969
texts.15:
## 1960-1969
### Datsun® 1600 Roadster
The Datsun 1600 Roadster debuted in 1964-1965 as the Datsun Fairlady 1500 and shared many mechanical features with the Datsun Bluebird. Eventually, the model evolved into the Fairlady 1600 Roadster.
The 70s were a great decade for Nissan. Nissan sold the one-millionth Datsun and became the top vehicle importer in the United States by 1975.
texts.16:
## NISSAN DESIGN COMES TO AMERICA
Driving innovation
In 1971, annual sales eclipsed 250,000 in the United States for the first time. Nissan also established itself on the track, as the now-legendary Datsun 510 and 240Z dominated racing on two continents. In 1973, the 1-Millionth Vehicle was sold in America. In 1979, Nissan Design America (NDA) was established in La Jolla, California, with a mandate to bring American style and concepts to Nissan vehicles. Over the years, NDA has brought us the original Altima®, the original Pathfinder®, the modular Pulsar NX, Xterra®.
texts.17:
## 1970-1979
Pushing the limits. Building a solid reputation
1971
texts.18:
## 1970-1979
### Datsun Coupe
The Datsun Coupe featured seating for five and "fold-down" rear seats. Available in the U.S. from 1970-73, selling 89,541 units making it the best-selling car of the time. Datsun 1200 Coupes won three SCCA C-Sedan National Championships.
1971
texts.19:
## 1970-1979
### Racing Datsun 510, #46
Peter Brock and Brock Racing Enterprises (BRE) built and raced the number 46 Datsun 510, which won the 1971 and 1972 SCCA Trans-Am championships driven by John Morton. Its success helped to bring brand recognition to a newcomer in the emerging Japanese market.
1971
texts.20:
## 1970-1979
### Datsun 240Z debut
240Z was introduced as a new sports car at the New York Auto Show in 1969. It featured a fastback styled body based on European design and boasted standard equipment, like a strong inline 2.4 liter 6-cylinder engine and full instrumentation reclining bucket seats at an affordable price.
1972
texts.21:
## 1970-1979
### Datsun 510® sedan
The 510® was a novel concept at the time: A good-looking, economical, fuel-efficient, five-passenger car that was fun to drive. It was available in a 4-door sedan or 2-door coupe with independent rear suspension or a 5-door wagon. Over its lifetime, the 510 went on to sell more than 300,000 units.
1977
texts.22:
## 1970-1979
### Datsun King Cab
Building a solid reputation for durable and fun-to-drive small trucks, Datsun introduced the King Cab, the first extended cab pickup, in 1977.
1978
texts.23:
## 1970-1979
### Datsun B210gx
The B210 was renowned as Nissan’s best-selling small sedan of the 1970s. The 1978 model was rated at 48 mpg highway, and the “B210 Plus” edition boasted 50 mpg highway – a lofty achievement for a carbureted vehicle.
texts.24:
## FROM TRUCKS TO THE RACETRACKS
Building off of success
Nissan built upon its successes of the 1970s – both in the showrooms and on the racetrack. Nissan Motor Manufacturing Corporation (NMMC) was established in Smyrna, Tennessee, to fulfill the growing demand for Nissan vehicles. In 1989, Nissan produced the 1-millionth vehicle on American soil. On the track, Hollywood legend Paul Newman captured Nissan's 50th national SCCA championship following consecutive wins in 1985 and 1986 with the Newman/Sharp Trans-Am 300ZX®.
texts.25:
## 1980-1989
Finding our stride, Building on racing legends.
1981
texts.26:
## 1980-1989
### 4-door Sports Car is born
The first-generation Nissan Maxima was introduced as the successor to the Datsun 810 sedan. Equipped with an inline-6 engine from the 240Z, this was no ordinary sedan and the Maxima cemented its 4-door sports car status for decades to come.
1982
texts.27:
## 1980-1989
### Championship off-road racing trucks
Between 1982 and 1992, Datsun collected an impressive 19 off-roading championship trophies.Nissan's most radical off-roader — a sandblasting 380-hp King Cab desert racer — competed in the HRDA/SCORE Class 1 Unlimited Vehicle series.
1983
texts.28:
## 1980-1989
### First American-built Nissan truck
The marketing of vehicles using Nissan badging in the U.S.began with the production of the 1984 Nissan pickup on June 16, 1983, at the new assembly plant in Smyrna, Tennessee. Early models carried dual Datsun-Nissan branding to help consumers make the change.
1985
texts.29:
## 1980-1989
### First Sentra® built in America
The first-generation Nissan Sentra was introduced in 1982 as a replacement for the popular and economical B210. It was so popular in the U.S. that in 1985, Sentra became the second Nissan model to roll off the line in the U.S in Smyrna, Tennessee.
1988
texts.30:
## 1980-1989
### The stellar Nissan racing record
Nissan racing driver Geoff Brabham won his first of four consecutive IMSA Camel GT Driver’s Championships. Brabham’s IMSA GTP ZX-T car was practically unbeatable that year, clocking a breathtaking top speed of 200+ miles per hour on several tracks and winning eight consecutive races.
texts.31:
## Leaping Into Green Tech
Retaining the best of Nissan
In 1991, Nissan received its first environmental award from the EPA,taking a big leap forward in green technology by lending its Alternative Fuel Vehicle to a California testing program and introducing the Future Electric Vehicle concept car. In 1997, Nissan was named “Best of the Best” by the Environmental Protection Agency. 1992 marked the sale of the 2-millionth Nissan Sentra in the United States, an additional accomplishment.
texts.32:
## 1990-1999
A decade of agility and innovation.
1993
texts.33:
## 1990-1999
### First Altima assembled in America
The Nissan Altima was introduced to replace the discontinued Stanza line. U.S.-assembled in Smyrna, Tennessee, it made an immediate impact in the mid-size sedan segment which continues today with its sixth-generation.
1995
texts.34:
## 1990-1999
### Compact without compromise
1995 was the year Nissan introduced the world to the all-new 200SX® coupe and the all-new 4th-generation Sentra.
1999
texts.35:
## 1990-1999
### The first 4-door compact truck
In 1999, Nissan introduced the Frontier® Crew Cab, the first compact truck with four full-sized doors. That same year, Frontier, Xterra® and Pathfinder® were named the official vehicles of the Los Angeles County lifeguards, which made many appearances in the T.V. show “Baywatch.”
GROWING LINE-UP
texts.36:
## 21st-Century thrills
Nissan nearly doubled the number of models offered and its sales. In 10 years, the diverse lineup grew to include the first full-size Nissan truck, along with all-new hybrid technology and a 21st-century supercar. And this is only the beginning of what's to come.
texts.38:
## 2000-2009
### Z Resurrected
The Nissan 350Z, a two-door, two-seater sports car, kicked off production in 2002 and ended the 6-year production hiatus in the US. Its sleek redesign of the 240Z DNA, rejuvenated the Nissan market presence throughout the decade.
2005
texts.39:
## 2000-2009
### Off-road innovation
An all-new midsize Frontier® launched with the most powerful V6 in its class. Nissan also introduced a mid-sized Pathfinder® with an added 3rd-row of seating, and the 2nd-generation Xterra® made its debut.
2007
texts.40:
## 2000-2009
### Nissan's first hybrid
In 2007, Nissan offered a hybrid driving option for the first time ever with the introduction of the all-new Altima® Hybrid.
2009
texts.41:
## 2000-2009
### The legend lands
Nissan brought its legendary GT-R to the U.S as an affordable supercar. With amazing acceleration, all-wheel drive, aggressive handling and bold styling, it has become an icon in the U.S. sports car market.
2009
texts.42:
## 2000-2009
### The shape of things
The boxy yet stylish Nissan Cube® made its North American debut with its non-traditional, asymmetrical body.
TRADITION OF INNOVATION
texts.43:
## The first Nissan EV
Nissan helped to lead the automotive industry into the age of electric vehicles when it debuted the all-electric Nissan LEAF®. Throughout the decade, Nissan continued its tradition of innovation that excites with all-new vehicles like the Nissan Kicks and with safety technology like its available Safety Shield® 360 suite of features.
texts.45:
## 2010-2020
### Nissan LEAF®
In 2010, Nissan introduced Nissan LEAF®—the world’s first mass-produced, 100% electric, zero-emission automobile. The standard 24-kWh battery was replaced with a 30-kWh battery for 2016, featuring 107 miles of range. The 2018 LEAF introduced an all-new design and a 40-kWh battery that took range up to 151 miles, and in 2019, LEAF PLUS added an available 60-kWh battery, estimated by EPA to offer up to 226 miles of range.
2018
texts.46:
## 2010-2020
### Nissan Kicks: The crossover of self expression
The Nissan Kicks made its North American debut as an affordable entry in the fast-growing subcompact crossover segment. Redesigned for 2025, the Kicks grew in size and adopted new styling inside and out, along with a more powerful engine and available Intelligent All-Wheel Drive.
2019
texts.47:
## 2010-2020
### Nissan Altima: All-Wheel Drive sedan
Continuing the Altima tradition of innovation in the sedan market, the Nissan Altima offered an available Intelligent All-Wheel Drive system for the first time. And it's still available today.
Nissan Goes Electric
texts.48:
## 2010-2020
### The All-Electric 2026 Nissan LEAF®
Discover a sleek, aerodynamic design engineered for efficiency and performance. Innovation meets power in every detail of this all-electric vehicle.

May 17, 2023
**NASHVILLE, Tenn.** – The story began on June 16, 1983, when the first Nissan manufactured in the U.S.− a white 720 pickup − rolled off the assembly line in Smyrna, marking the genesis of automotive production in Tennessee.
Nissan has since expanded its U.S. footprint to include a powertrain plant in Decherd, Tennessee in 1997 and a vehicle assembly plant in Canton, Mississippi in 2003. Collectively, these facilities have proudly built 1 nearly 20 million vehicles and 13 million engines in the U.S. for customers around the globe.
"What began with one pickup truck has turned into four decades of manufacturing excellence," said Nissan Americas Chairperson Jérémie Papin. "This milestone isn't just about the products we've built and sold over the past 40 years. It's also about applauding Nissan's more than 21,000 U.S. employees who will take us into our future − our electrified future − and continue to enhance our products and services for customers."
**Stronger communities**
Nissan prides itself on being supportive of its neighbors and helping to build stronger communities. Over the past 40 years, the company and its manufacturing team members have positively impacted communities through charitable contributions and volunteerism, including:
*   **43,000** volunteer hours  
*   **38**homes constructed with Habitat for Humanity  
*   Nearly **$26,000,000** in United Way donations  
*   Nearly **$2,000,000** in educational scholarships  
*   **36,000** pints of blood donated to the American Red Cross
**Electrified future**

# 40 years of people, product and purpose
The vehicles of the near future are connected and electric. Nissan is supporting that transition by building factories of the future today as part of its long-term vision, Ambition 2030**, which includes plans for 27 electrified models globally, including 19 all-electric vehicles, by 2030.**
**In 2022, Nissan**announced**a $500 million investment to transform its**Canton, Mississippi facility into a center for U.S. EV production to support two all-new, all-electric vehicles in 2025. This investment is one of several the company is planning in the U.S. over the next five years, supporting its target of 40% of U.S. vehicle sales to be fully electric, by 2030.
To learn more about Nissan's U.S. manufacturing operations, visit the company's newly launched website www.NissanManufacturing.com.
